_comment: SKILL BLUEPRINT SCHEMA — output of the Spec agent, input to the Generator agent.
_comment2: One blueprint per standard. This is the contract the generator builds against.
subject: math
cluster: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems
description: Students compute unit rates where the rate itself is a ratio of fractions — e.g., (3/4 mile) per (1/2 hour) — by dividing complex fractions. They must set up the rate correctly, apply fraction division, and express the result with appropriate units.
subSkills: Set up a ratio of two quantities given in fraction form
Divide a fraction by a fraction (multiply by the reciprocal)
Identify and label units correctly in the unit rate
Apply unit rate reasoning to real-world contexts (speed, price per unit, density)

problemArchetypes.name: Distance/time
problemArchetypes.example: A car travels 3/4 mile in 1/4 hour. What is the speed in miles per hour?

problemArchetypes.name: Price per unit
problemArchetypes.example: A store sells 2/3 pound of cheese for $5/4. What is the cost per pound?

problemArchetypes.name: Area/time or work rate
problemArchetypes.example: A painter covers 5/6 of a wall in 2/3 of an hour. How much wall per hour?

problemArchetypes.name: Density or concentration
problemArchetypes.example: A solution contains 3/8 gram of salt in 1/4 liter. What is the concentration in grams per liter?

Easy.description: One of the two quantities is a whole number or simple unit fraction (1/2, 1/3, 1/4). The division step is straightforward with no simplification required beyond reducing once.
constraints: Denominator of the complex fraction is a unit fraction (1/n)

Medium.description: Both quantities are non-unit fractions. Requires full fraction division and simplification. May involve mixed numbers or slightly larger values.
constraints: Both numerator and denominator of the complex fraction are non-unit fractions
Context may be less familiar (density, work rate)

Hard.description: Multi-step: student must first convert or set up the complex fraction from a verbal description before computing. May involve comparison of two unit rates or a follow-up question.
constraints: Requires reading comprehension to extract the two quantities
May involve mixed numbers that must be converted to improper fractions first
Follow-up asks student to compare two unit rates or find a total

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student adds or subtracts the fractions instead of dividing
Student divides in the wrong order (denominator ÷ numerator)
Student multiplies straight across without taking the reciprocal
Student forgets to attach units to the answer
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Gives '3/2' instead of '3/2 miles per hour'

_comment_itemCounts: New material model. worksheet.single = one ramped sheet (Easy->Hard across 15 items). worksheet.tier1/tier2 = the two sheets of a complex (two-worksheet) standard (15 each; tier1 Easy->Medium, tier2 Medium->Hard, no item overlap). Most standards use a single worksheet. Cluster materials have no per-standard blueprint; their counts (cluster-worksheet 15, cluster-test 12) are enforced by check.mjs defaults.
